summary.headline: Registering a GitHub OAuth App is instant and self-serve, but GitHub prefers GitHub Apps, and organization owners can restrict OAuth apps.
summary.type_note: Registration is self-serve with no GitHub review. If an organization enforces an application policy, an organization owner must authorize your OAuth app for that organization.

difficulty_factors.reason: Direct self-service form in user/organization developer settings.
GitHub does not review OAuth apps for registration, but organizations can require owner approval before an app can access their data.
No fee is mentioned in the registration documentation.
You must log in to create the app and get credentials; organization owners may need to approve it.

approval_wait.label: None for registration; an organization owner may need to approve use on organization data

can_start_today.reason: Registration is fully self-service and available immediately upon logging into GitHub.

confidence.reason: Registration steps and scopes come from GitHub's docs, but the authorize-endpoint probe was inconclusive and some limits (such as how many OAuth apps one account can create) could not be confirmed.

blockers.title: Organization owners may need to approve your app
blockers.detail: When an organization has an application access policy, only an organization owner can authorize an OAuth app for that organization. Your users who belong to such organizations may be unable to grant access until an owner approves.
blockers.workaround: Ask the user's organization owner to approve the app, and explain which scopes you request.

blockers.title: GitHub recommends GitHub Apps over OAuth apps
blockers.detail: GitHub says GitHub Apps are generally preferred: fine-grained permissions, short-lived tokens, and rate limits that scale. OAuth apps use broad scopes and the user's rate limit.
blockers.workaround: Decide between the two before registering. This guide covers OAuth apps.

steps.title: Decide: OAuth app or GitHub App
steps.action: GitHub generally prefers GitHub Apps for new integrations (fine-grained permissions, short-lived tokens, scalable rate limits). This guide covers OAuth apps; decide before you register.

steps.title: Navigate to Developer Settings
steps.action: Log in to GitHub, click your profile picture in the upper-right corner, select Settings, click Developer settings in the left sidebar, and then click OAuth apps.
steps.why_human_only: Requires authentication into a personal GitHub account.

steps.title: Register New OAuth App
steps.action: Click 'New OAuth App' (or 'Register a new application') and fill in your application details.
steps.why_human_only: Requires interactive form submission and authenticated session.

fields.name: Application name
fields.guidance: Enter your AI agent's public name (e.g., {{app_name}}).

fields.name: Homepage URL
fields.guidance: Enter the full URL to your application's homepage (e.g., {{homepage_url}}).

steps.title: Retrieve Credentials
steps.action: Copy the generated Client ID and generate a new Client Secret, then store them securely in your app environment.
steps.why_human_only: Secrets are displayed once and require authenticated access to view.

steps.title: If a user's organization restricts apps, request owner approval
steps.action: Ask the organization owner to approve your OAuth app under the organization's third-party application settings, then retry authorization.
steps.why_human_only: Only an organization owner can approve the app for that organization.

scopes.purpose: Broad access to repositories, including issues, pull requests and anything repository-owned. OAuth apps cannot request narrower repository permissions, so ask for this only if you need it.
Reads and writes all user profile data including private profile info.

common_rejection_reasons.reason: A user in an organization with an app access policy cannot authorize your app
common_rejection_reasons.fix: Ask an organization owner to approve the app for the organization.

you_must.task: Log into GitHub and create the OAuth App via Developer Settings
you_must.reason: Requires human authentication and account ownership.

you_must.task: Securely save Client ID and Client Secret
you_must.reason: Credentials must be kept confidential and cannot be retrieved by automated agents.

evidence.claim: You can create and register an OAuth app under your personal account or organization via Settings > Developer settings > OAuth apps > New OAuth App.
evidence.source_note: Official instructions for creating an OAuth app on GitHub.

evidence.claim: GitHub OAuth apps use explicit scopes such as repo and user to define requested access permissions.
evidence.source_note: Official documentation detailing available OAuth scopes.

evidence.claim: GitHub generally prefers GitHub Apps over OAuth apps; OAuth apps need the repo scope for issues and pull requests, and tokens use the user's rate limit.
evidence.source_note: GitHub's comparison of GitHub Apps and OAuth apps.

evidence.claim: When an organization application policy is active, only an organization owner can authorize an OAuth app for the organization.
evidence.source_note: Same comparison page, section on who can install or authorize.

unknowns.question: Is there a limit on how many OAuth apps one account or organization can create?

unknowns.how_to_resolve: Check GitHub's developer settings page or documentation.
